detail.longDescription: According to PEP 8 , class names should use the UpperCamelCase (CapWords) convention. However, I have seen classes use lowercase names. For example, in the standard library: class socket(_socket.socket): ... class defaultdict(dict): ... PEP 8 also says: The naming convention for functions may be used instead in cases where the interface is documented and used primarily as a callable. All classes are callable as they can be instantiated. So what does that sentence mean? Putting aside builtin types, when and why would it be desirable to use a non-CapWords class name?
